text:
Noor (PM): dropped a tiny experiment for the scorecard selection flow. main asks: microcopy for bulk actions, keyboard focus behavior when details rail is open, and SR announcements. figma: https://figma.com/selection-flow Kai (Design): thinking about the primary CTA copy. Options: "Approve results" vs "Approve selection" when rows are selected. Also wondering if the CTA should show the count inline like "Approve (3)". Thoughts? :thinking_face: Marta (Eng): inline count is fine but be careful updating it frequently — spamming DOM updates while users keyboard-navigate can be noisy for SRs. we should debounce count updates and push them into an aria-live polite region rather than changing the button label every tap. Lars (QA): repro from current build: when you open the details rail, Tab moves into the rail and the selection checkbox loses visible focus. users get stuck because Esc closes rail but focus doesn't return to the checkbox. expected: close rail -> focus returns to the previously focused row/checkbox. Jo (Accessibility): agree with Lars. pattern: save the last focused element id before opening rail, and restore focus on close with focus({preventScroll:true}). also: provide a skip link at top: "Skip to run summary" that jumps to an aria-live summary. Noor (PM): microcopy rule: avoid ambiguous verbs. prefer "Approve selections" when multiple rows selected, and "Approve result" only on single-sample detail view. Tooltip copy for disabled state: "Select one or more samples to approve". Kai (Design): visual variant: display CTA as "Approve (n)" when n>0 and show a subtle badge. when n=0 show "Approve selections" disabled. ensure contrast for badge. Marta (Eng): implementation plan: don't mutate label text for SR users, instead announce count changes via
Selected 3 samples
. button label remains stable to avoid surprise. Jo (Accessibility): that's good. also add offscreen text for the CTA describing scope: e.g., Approve selected 3 samples in this run. and use aria-pressed on toggle-ish controls where applicable. Lars (QA): keyboard matrix notes: Arrow nav between rows, Space or Enter toggles selection, cmd+Enter opens quick-approve modal (confirm), Esc closes modals and returns focus to the last row. when details rail is open, LeftArrow should close it and restore focus. I'll add these to the ticket. Noor (PM): should quick-approve bypass the modal if a user enabled a preference? We have an "auto-confirm" toggle in settings. If on, cmd+Enter should act immediately but still provide an accessible toast that is focusable via a View results link. Marta (Eng): good call. sample aria-live toast snippet:
Approved 3 samples. View results
Make sure the toast link is keyboard focusable and does not auto-steal focus. Jo (Accessibility): ensure toasts are reachable via a list of announcements or a dedicated toast region that SR users can focus into. also provide clear textual result labels instead of icons: e.g., "2 regressions, 1 flaky". Kai (Design): small visual tweak: when a user selects many rows (>50) show an infobar: "Selecting many samples may take longer to approve. Continue?" with a subtle CTA. This can be a progressive disclosure pattern rather than a modal. Lars (QA): test plan: focus trapping scenarios, SR readouts for aria-live regions, toast link navigation, and restore-focus flows. I'll include NVDA/VoiceOver steps. Marta (Eng): rough estimate: 2 dev days to implement restore-focus + aria-live selection announcements + toast link behavior, 1 QA day. I'll open a draft PR with code snippets for focus restore and the polite live region. Noor (PM): next steps: Kai iterate microcopy with badge variant, Marta prototype PR, Jo/Lars to draft acceptance checks. scheduled 15-min check-in tomorrow 9am PT. cc @ux-bot for checklist :white_check_mark: ux-bot: checklist created: [Microcopy badge frames], [Focus restore impl PR], [A11y acceptance tests], [QA keyboard matrix]. Noor (PM): final note: keep the button label stable for SRs, use polite live announcements for dynamic counts, restore focus on close, and avoid toasts that steal focus. thanks! :raised_hands:
